title: The USA Pavilion at Specialized Expo 2027 in Belgrade, Serbia, Announces Theme
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 12, 2026

In May 2026, the United States confirmed its participation in Specialized Expo 2027 in Belgrade, Serbia.  The theme of Expo 2027 is “Play for Humanity – Sports and Music for All” and asks international participants to highlight sports and music in their pavilions.  As is tradition for International Expositions, each pavilion will have its own theme to celebrate its country’s unique take on the overall subject.
The USA Pavilion is pleased to announce its theme:  “Freedom to Play.”  This theme celebrates the liberty that empowers Americans to compete, innovate, and strive for excellence in all arenas, but especially sports and music.  Through its exhibits and programming, the USA Pavilion will highlight longstanding U.S. leadership in sports and music.  It will offer six exhibits, a live performance stage, and a roadhouse-style restaurant that will give visitors a chance to experience American culture.  
Expo 2027 is a historic opportunity for the United States to continue strengthening its partnership with Serbia.  Through its participation and the USA Pavilion, the United States will capitalize on Expo 2027 convening opportunities to promote U.S. culture, values, and commercial initiatives.
For further information, please email expo@state.gov or contact us on our website at https://usapavilion.us/.  For media inquiries, please submit here.

title: Assistant Secretary Weiland Delivers New Tools to Counter Narcoterrorism in Ecuador
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 12, 2026

Assistant Secretary of State for International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) F. Cartwright Weiland traveled to Ecuador November 2–7, 2026, to deepen cooperation against the narcoterrorists and transnational criminal organizations that threaten both our nations.  The Assistant Secretary’s visit built on the $55 million in INL assistance that Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced in Ecuador in September, including $45 million to dismantle narcoterrorist groups and $10 million to combat illegal gold mining, gang recruitment, illicit finance, and maritime drug trafficking.
In Galápagos, Assistant Secretary Weiland transferred a 38-foot interceptor boat to the Ecuadorian Navy.  This was the latest of 14 interceptors INL is providing to Ecuador’s Navy and National Police to help them intercept drug traffickers, disrupt illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing, and stop drugs at sea before they reach the United States and harm American communities.
In Quito, Assistant Secretary Weiland and Ecuadorian officials signed an agreement that gives Ecuador’s Financial and Economic Analysis Unit (UAFE) access to advanced data analytics technology from U.S. company Palantir.  Using this cutting-edge American technology, UAFE will better identify illicit financial networks, support money laundering prosecutions, and cut off narcoterrorists’ illicit profits that fund violence and corruption.
To strengthen the National Police’s ability to prevent and investigate kidnappings and extortion, Assistant Secretary Weiland and Minister of Interior John Reimberg renewed an agreement signed in 2024.  Since then, the Ecuadorian police’s anti-kidnapping and anti-extortion unit has worked closely with the U.S. Embassy and Consulate to rescue eight U.S. citizens.  Protecting American citizens is one of President Trump’s top priorities, and this renewed partnership will help keep Americans in Ecuador safe.
The Assistant Secretary and Ministry of Interior also signed a declaration of intent to combat illicit gold trafficking, a major source of revenue for narcoterrorist groups.

title: Under Secretary for Arms Control and International Security Thomas G. DiNanno Advances Security Cooperation with Peru and Colombia
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 12, 2026

Under Secretary for Arms Control and International Security Thomas G. DiNanno traveled to Peru and Colombia from November 1–7, 2026, advancing U.S. security cooperation with both countries against drug trafficking and narcoterrorism, as well as civil nuclear cooperation with Peru.
The Under Secretary met with Peru’s defense minister, vice foreign minister, and vice interior minister to discuss efforts to improve defense and security coordination for combatting foreign terrorist organizations and transnational criminal organizations in Peru and the region.  He announced that the United States provided $20 million in Fiscal Year 2026 Foreign Military Financing (FMF) to build Peru’s F-16 aerial refueling capability, extending the range and effectiveness of Peru’s fighter fleet.  He also announced the United States provided $4.5 million in prior-year FMF for the design phase of the Port of Callao infrastructure program, which he visited to see U.S. support and progress for modernization and port security projects.
In Peru, Under Secretary DiNanno opened the inaugural bilateral Foundational Infrastructure for Responsible Use of Small Modular Reactor Technology (FIRST) workshop, announcing the United States will provide Peru with $1 million in funding under the FIRST program.  This funding will enable Peru to utilize tailored U.S. technical assistance and training on nuclear safety, security, nonproliferation, regulatory development, stakeholder engagement, and workforce development to enable potential deployment of small modular reactors or microreactors.
Under Secretary DiNanno also signed a Nuclear Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding (NCMOU) between the United States and Peru with Minister of Energy and Mines Guillermo Shinno.  The NCMOU is an important step toward a lasting civil nuclear partnership between the two countries and establishes a framework for deepened cooperation as Peru pursues a domestic program aligned with the highest standards of nuclear safety, security, and nonproliferation.  As Under Secretary DiNanno stated in his remarks before the NCMOU signing, “By choosing the United States as its civil nuclear partner, Peru gains access to world-leading American technology, decades of proven regulatory and technical expertise, and a long-term partner who will support Peru at every stage from planning to deployment.”   In line with President Trump’s agenda to advance American nuclear energy, the United States is expanding grant financing under Executive Order 14299 for American nuclear technology pilots, fuel supplies, and project preparation in partner economies of strategic interest.
In Colombia, Under Secretary DiNanno met with Colombian defense and justice ministers, the vice foreign minister, and the National Police director during which he recognized the important counternarcotics and security results that President Abelardo de la Espriella’s government has achieved in its first three months.  The Under Secretary noted Colombia’s success taking narcoterrorist leaders off the battlefield and signing extradition orders, while also supporting Colombia’s commitment to significantly increase coca eradication and cocaine interdiction.  The Trump Administration looks forward to Colombia continuing to make significant progress in reducing cocaine production and trafficking and dismantling narcoterrorist organizations.
The Under Secretary presided over the delivery of firearms training simulators at the International Police Training School of Colombia (CENOP).  This specialized American-made equipment will enable police from Colombia and regional partners to hone skills to take down narcoterrorist networks that threaten American citizens.
Under Secretary DiNanno met with U.S. and Colombian troops participating in the Southern Vanguard exercise, which brings together approximately 800 participants to build readiness and strengthen our shared response to regional threats.
